module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 817

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/817](https://www.erdosproblems.com/817)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos817

/-- Define $g_k(n)$ to be the minimal $N$ such that $\{1, ..., N\}$ contains some $A$ of
size $|A| = n$ such that
$$
  \langle A\rangle = \left\{\sum_{a \in A} \epsilon_a a : \epsilon_a \in\{0, 1\}\right\}
$$
contains no non-trivial $k$-term arithmetic progression. -/
noncomputable
def g (k : ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ := sInf { N | ∃ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, A.card = n ∧
    ∀ s, s ⊆ { ∑ a ∈ B, a | B ∈ A.powerset } → s.IsAPOfLengthFree k}

/-- Let $k \geq 3$. Define $g_k(n)$ to be the minimal $N$ such that
$\{1, ..., N\}$ contains some $A$ of size $|A| = n$ such that
$$
  \langle A\rangle = \left\{\sum_{a \in A} \epsilon_a a : \epsilon_a \in\{0, 1\}\right\}
$$
contains no non-trivial $k$-term arithmetic progression. Estimate $g_k(n)$. In
particular, is it true that
$$
  g_3(n) \gg 3^n
$$ -/
-- Formalisation note : only formalising the "In particular" part
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_817 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ (fun n => (3 ^ n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n => (g 3 n : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/-- A problem of Erdős and Sárközy who proved
$$
  g_3(n) \gg \frac{3^n}{n^{O(1)}}.
$$ -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_817.variants.bdd_power : ∃ O > (0 : ℝ),
    (fun (n : ℕ) => (3 ^ n : ℝ) / n ^ O) =O[atTop] fun n => (g 3 n : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos817

status_issues.recorded: @[category research open], with answer(sorry); explicitly formalizes only the question g₃(n) ≫ 3ⁿ.
status_issues.source_status: Costa’s source-linked September 2026 preprint gives a negative answer to this specific subquestion: Corollary 1.2 states liminf g₃(n)/3ⁿ = 0. The general estimation problem remains open. Qualification: erdosproblems.com currently presents Costa’s result as an unverified partial proof claim, rather than marking the overall problem solved.
status_issues.evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.06303, submitted 5 September 2026; Corollary 1.2 explicitly says: “there do not exist constants c>0 and n₀ such that g₃(n)≥c3ⁿ for every n≥n₀.” The result is linked in https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/discuss/817 and listed as a partial proof claim at https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/817/proof-claims.
status_issues.suggested_change: Review acceptance of Costa’s result for a status update of this declaration alone. If accepted, change its category to research solved and replace answer(sorry) with answer(False), citing Corollary 1.2. Do not mark the broader estimation problem fully solved.

reformulations.difference: The definition requires every subset s of the subset-sum set to be k-AP-free, rather than directly requiring the subset-sum set itself to be k-AP-free.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any set S, (∀ s ⊆ S, s.IsAPOfLengthFree k) ↔ S.IsAPOfLengthFree k. The forward implication takes s = S. Conversely, any arithmetic progression contained in a subset of S is contained in S, so progression-freeness is hereditary. Thus the extra quantifier does not change the admissible sets or the minimum defining g.

review.notes: All three declarations were checked. Scratch Lean proofs establish the hereditary reformulation, the equivalence of natural-number 3-AP-freeness with ThreeAPFree, both Big-O-to-positive-lower-bound translations, and g₃(0)=0, g₃(1)=1, g₃(2)=3, g₃(3)=8. The powers-of-three construction guarantees that the defining minimum exists in the relevant domain; sInf ∅ is therefore not reached. The real-power denominator at n=0 is harmless under atTop. The polynomial-loss variant faithfully states the source’s established bound. Experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/ap_boundary.lean; the reviewed file was not modified.
